title: What Have I  Learned  Living in Stina?

data.text: Many people opt for spending the whole life in a place where they were born. However some decide to take a risk and experience something completely different. What do they do? They move in order to explore and to see how others do the things with the intention to discover something better or appreciate things they have more. For the same reason I made up my mind to join a volunteering project in Ukraine which includes working in a rural area, namely a village called Stina. This place has become very attractive for young guys from different countries who want to push their limits and obtain a unique experience. Locals are already used to seeing German or Turkish, French or Italian guys walking around. Furthermore, they are enthusiastic to interract with the foreigners, take part in different activities all togeter and, I would say, that creates the atmosphere of international unity in Stina.

Personally I was quite scared of living in a village. Can you imagine moving from a city full of skyscrapers (Kuala Lumpur) to Stina where only a few hundreds of people live. However, I was willing to face the challenge because every adventure in life has its beauty. In the beginning the village seemed very small to me and I was disappointed by bad roads. Soon my perspective changed completely. I was surprised how much I enjoyed myself there and noticed a lot of positive sides. First of all, locals are really good people, it's a great pleasure to communicate with them even though we don't speak the same language. Secondly, it gives the opportunity to obtain a lot of skills and knowledge especially concerning environmental protection Where else could I learn how to construct a wind turbine? And the most pleasant parts are nights at the campfire. As for me, no entertainment a city offers can compare to those simple moments. The quietness of night always surprised me and gave me inner peace. In addition, intersting conversation with amazing people. Especially I liked listening to Yarik, the leader of our organisation. He has a lot of stories to tell about previous volunteers and maybe one day he will tell stories about me, too. Who knows?

I really loved the village life in Stina. It was a great experience where I learned a lot about life itself. I’m grateful for this opportunity and I would recommend everyone to try such a lifestyle at least once in a lifetime.

title: Intercultural dialogue among volunteers of Vinnytsia

data.text: One of the greatest benefits of the European Solidarity Corps volunteering program is that it provides an intercultural environment for volunteers coming all over Europe. Volunteers find an opportunity to engage with others and learn their culture directly from them which helps to overcome prejudices. This engagement between volunteers proves that we are much more similar than what it is used to show on social media or television. The reason for this supposed to be social media and communication channels focuses on government relations not the dialogue of people. And what volunteering projects do is to bring all different kinds of nationalities together so they can see how much can be done when this occurs.

What I experienced working with friends from the Netherlands, Italy, France, Germany and Ukraine during my time in Pangeya Ultima is quite valuable for me as it made me understand the meaning of the word “solidarity” written in the project title given by the EU commission. I understood that Solidarity makes us able to do so much more than what we would do by being only one. Therefore, we were able to make lots of different projects by using our creativity and skills that occurred thanks to being in a multicultural environment. To mention a few of the activities that we have done. Once I remember we organized a festival in Voronovytsia where we were able to create different cultural activities such as a theatre, a Ukrainian traditional dance performance, a photo exhibition and so on.

Being around volunteers from all over Europe also provided me to learn personal skills from my colleagues such as I understood well the cultures of the Netherlands, Italy, France and so on. I remember quite well I learned how to cook an Italian coffee from my mate Matteo and also never order a pizza with pineapples on top of it :), Dutch people are always on time and well planned. I think these are the cultural info that can be only learned by having a direct intercultural dialogue, so I feel very lucky to be a volunteer in a place where I had a great example of intercultural dialogue.

Furthermore, I had also chances to talk about my nationality and my cultural background with my mates from different backgrounds. I believe it was a great chance to see what my cultural background is like from my perspective. I shared some cuisine of Turkey and tried to teach them to other volunteers. I should also mention that I had a lot of questions coming from people about Turkey and I answered them and informed people what it looked like in reality. Therefore, it was also a great chance for me to improve myself in terms of intercultural dialogue competence.

In conclusion, being in Vinnytsia for over a half year gave me to understand the basics of intercultural dialogue and also solidarity exists over this dialogue. I believe that these volunteering opportunities will enhance community engagement internationally and locally.
Ibrahim Tamer

title: Interview with professor Mr. Petruk about climate change

data.text: Climate change is a global crisis that threatens our planet, our societies and our economies, and it also requires needed effective measures. And Ukraine is quite vulnerable to the impacts of climate change. It is the air quality, but also the broader effects of droughts, high temperatures, heat waves and floods. These sorts of extreme climate events are now more likely and severe in Ukraine than ever before. For learning more about climate change and other environmental problems in Ukraine, we decided to meet with Mr. Petruk. Mr. Petruk is a professor in department of Ecology at Vinnytsia Technical University. He has been researching about climate change and its effects on the planet for years. He accepted our offer to give an interview and answer our questions. First he gave some information about climate change and its impact on Ukraine; he said that Ukraine is a large, diverse country with high agricultural potential, rich natural resources, and an established industrial base. Climate-driven changes such as higher temperatures – causing potential shifts in agricultural zones and leading to marked water deficiencies – can compromise the country’s food security and economic growth. The vulnerability of the population, which is largely urban, is magnified by infrastructure deficiencies such as an aging and fragile housing stock and limited potable water supply. The energy sector was responsible for nearly all of the greenhouse gas emissions, followed by manufacturing and construction, fugitive emissions, other fuel combustion, and transportation.

He also mentioned how important to decrease level of carbon on air. He also explained the definition of decorbanisation. Decarbonisation is the reduction of carbon dioxide emissions through the use of low carbon power sources, achieving a lower output of greenhouse gasses into the atmosphere. He added: like many other countries, Ukraine has pledged to cut down its carbon emissions, but how this will be achieved remains unclear. Coal has long been an important source of power for Ukrainian industry, constituting about one-third of total primary energy supply. However, the ongoing quest for decarbonization is pushing the state to radically reduce emissions and find new energy options to support the Ukrainian economy.

When we asked about the usage of renewable energy in Ukraine; he said that Ukraine is a natural gas and petroleum liquids transit country between Russia and elsewhere in Europe, but higher ambient air temperatures lower efficiency of gas distribution systems. Ukraine has made significant renewable energy progress in recent years. Renewable energy – mostly hydropower – provides about 4 percent of energy but Ukraine’s National Renewable Energy Action Plan sets a target of 11 percent renewables in total energy consumption by 2020. If shale gas exploration in Ukraine’s eastern regions – interrupted by conflict – expands, it may compete for water with other needs. Coastal erosion also puts stress on oil/gas infrastructure.

Other question was about future of ecosystem and forests under impacts of climate change in Ukraine. First he showed some slides about how temperature is increasing year by year and it affects all living creatures in ecosystem. Unfortunately if we don't take any precautionary measures the temperature will increase to 4,5 degree by 2030. Moreover the fact that Ukraine is a home to 36 percent of Europe’s biodiversity, Ukraine’s ecosystems are varied. Impacts of climate change are of particular concern for rare species in the Danube Delta and the Carpathian Mountains. The increasing temperature is contributing fire risk which threatens the increasingly desiccated, nonnative spruce forests in the Carpathians, forests in the Chernobyl exclusion zone and pine forests of the Dnieper region. Pollution, overfishing, alien species, destruction of habitats and river reservoirs have reduced the industrial fishing potential of the Azov and Black Seas and damaged their marine ecosystems, masking climate change effects. However, absolute sea levels rose from 1992 – 2013 by 1 to 3 mm or more, increasing vulnerability of coastal areas to erosion and flooding.

After having an interview with Professor, once again we all understood that climate change is real and it is affecting our lives in different aspects. So one of the most important things is being aware of our actions and stopping this devastating concern by working together. I think Ukraine has a potential to achieve its sustainable development goals by cooperating and working internationally in near future.

I wanted to discover another culture, a new language. Why not a country of ex-USSR which hangs the shadow of a total war against Russia?
Yes, Ukraine seems like a good choice to me, everybody has doubts before a long trip, but now that I'm there, let's go for an adventure.

During my trip, once out of the airport, it became difficult to find English-speaking Ukrainians, but they are really nice people, so much so that a taxi man helped me to find the bus stop, someone in the train helped me find my place (it's harder than you think). Special mention to this super nice girl who helped me catch my train to Kyiv and took me to Puzata hata to discover Ukrainian food.

Finally I arrived in Vinnytsia. I am welcomed by Yaroslav and his smile. I already have a class about Vinnytsia, a small town with a very interesting history, architecture, aviation, navy. There is a lot to discover.

Now installed in a nice apartment with two other volunteers, I have a week of intense information about the organization. The Pangeya Ultima team, the volunteers are all very nice. They help me integrate. There is a really good atmosphere, it feels like i’m home.

Life in another country, another culture, the simplest things are a challenge like trying to weigh apples with another alphabet than yours. But no problem, only solutions when I speak with a merchant who speaks English as well as I do Ukrainian, we still manage to communicate and they know how to share their good mood.

Coming from a very rural and introverted background, in the week I've been here I've been to more restaurants and cafes than in my entire life. In Vinnytsia you can touch all cultures and visit the whole world.

I am under the spell of this pretty little town, I feel alive again, it's a new important chapter in my life that is beginning, I have no doubt that it will bring me a lot. I look forward to better understanding the Ukrainian people, their language and their culture. Look forward to contributing to the actions of Pangeya Ultima. I've been here for a week and I already want to say Дякую Вінниця.

title: Capturing the street musicians of Vinnytsia on video

data.text:
Coming from Leipzig, Germany, for me street music was always an integral part of walking through the streets, first and foremost in the city center. So obviously I was delighted, when, already in my first days, I saw a trumpetist playing odessan music near the water tower or when I saw a guitarrist going through the tram and singing, something that I have never seen before. So in mid september, I set out to capture some of the talented people, performing their music in the streets and bringing a joyful spirit to the city. Luckily, Jules, my french flatmate, agreed to help me by taking the role of the cameraman.
First of all, we obviously had to find them playing on the streets, which was my first unexpected challange. As soon as I was planning on filming them, they seemed to have dissapeared, completely vanished from the face of the earth as soon as I planned on capturing them on camera. For almost 3 weeks I was desperately hoping on finding them, without any succes. As I was losing hope it just so happened that I found three cool guys: Igor, the trumpetist I mentionned at the beginning; Valeri, a very sweet, elderly blind man playing the violin; and Igor, a very talented guy singing and playing guitar.
But there was another challenge I still had to overcome: my lack of self-discipline. This would haunt me for longer than I expected. Coming to an agreement about the time and place to film them was the easier part and filming them was really fun and interesting for us. Especially when one (slightly drunk) friend of Igor, the guitarist, came to us and while filming, was also talking to us, as well as helping us to get the perfect shot. It was one of my funniest experiences in Ukraine.

So once we got everything recorded, I had to compose a piece where interview parts and footage of the musicians music would intertwine and play together into one huge audio-visual symphony; in other words, I had to edit the footage.
And this is where my lack of discipline posed the biggest obstacle to my progress. Maybe it was also the sheer amount of footage, in total almost 2 hours, which I had to compress into a 10 minute long video, that intimidated me. So for a month or even longer I was procrastinating to edit the video, saying to myself that I deserve a bit of rest after having filmed them all. And only in december, when also the musicians started to ask how long it would be until the video would be finished, did I actually start to review the footage, from there would start the long, diffictult but also interesting journey of editing this video. About the process itself there is nothing much to tell, it was monotonous and sometimes also tedious, as it was the first time that I was working with an advanced video editing program, but nevertheless, I learned some new technical skills, which really satisfied me. And monotonous it may have been, but seeing your end product getting longer and putting your creativity and ideas into practise was really motivating. Watching the first complete part of your own video, adding subtitles and thinking: "Huh, it looks really cool!" was very pleasent.
So the work came to an end, after several weeks of editing, it was finally time to publish it, send it to the musicians, showing it to your friends and family and being proud of yourself, maybe not of the speed in which you did it, but the of the final product. it. I can actually look back and realize that I learned new things and skills and also that in truth I had a lot of great moments.

title: Europe's heritage in the hands of young people? - YES!

data.text: What can a group of youth from different countries do for the cultural heritage of one country? It turns out you simply need to understand the value of heritage, add some freedom of action and the result is incredible!

On September, 30 young people from Ukraine, Lithuania and Italy gathered in the Kamariškės manor in Zarasai district, Lithuania to participate in the international youth exchange project "European Heritage in the Hands of Youth". They worked on the topic of cultural heritage by searching for innovative ways of attracting visitors to cultural heritage sites and giving historical sites a new meaning in today's world.

During eight days the young people got to know each other, discussed the importance of cultural heritage for the present, and generated ideas on how to preserve and revitalize the endangered heritage sites. On the youth exchange participants had meetings with specialists in various fields and took part in some practical activities. Šarūnas Subatavičius - a local historian, presented the historical development of Kamariškės manor, and naturalist Žydrūnas Sinkevičius conducted an excursion in the territory of the manor. Many rare species of plants and animals live here in the historic park and in the old ponds.

The young people realized that not only the buildings are valuable, but the entire environment of the manor is extremely important for biodiversity. They even spent two days doing practical restoration works on the manor and biodiversity preservation: digging a "fridge" (here will be a wintering place for amphibians), pruning an apple tree in the garden, thinning some shrubs. After having the work done participants had a great idea - they suggested setting up a cognitive trail in the manor to present the values of the Kamariškės manor for the public and tourists. So they started to work on it in three teams for creating info boards: layout designers, board makers and writers.

The first team - layout designers, was working together with Karolina Želve, a professional cultural heritage interpreter, and their task was to organize the position and visual look of the stands in such a way that it will be interesting for the visitor to check them out. The second group - board makers, were actually making info boards with their own hands with the help of local wood craftsmen from the Innovators Valley. And the third team - writers, were responsible for collecting information to present on info boards and finalizing the text. They discovered the surroundings of Kamariškės manor and met locals who shared interesting stories.

After 8 days of intensive development and work, the young people managed to create, build up and establish a tour path in the vicinity of Kamariškės manor. Working together, participants exchanged ideas, planned and designed a cognitive trail, collected lots of information, learned to use special tools for working with wood, and created information stands. On the last day, together with cultural and nature activists, they organized an event for the local community and visitors of the manor, where they were happy to present the results of the youth exchange and new horizons for historic places in modern perspective.

title: ESC “Open Garden Camp” in Antaliepte, Lithuania

data.text: Opportunity: European Solidarity Corps “Open Garden Camp”
Location: Antaliepte, Lithuania
Hosting Organization: Innovators' Valley

Innovators’ valley invites you to participate at the “Open Garden Camp” in Antaliepte, a small village in the middle of the lake region of Lithuania. We are looking for 3 people from Ukraine with the spirit of adventure and open-minded, who want to experience community life, be creative and design a new open-air space in an inspiring place.
About organization:

Innovators' valley is restoring and developing unique cultural heritage - as a XVIIth century monastery -, and a beautiful surrounding - 12 hectares of park-. Step by step they are developing this historical and natural place as social innovations, environmental and non-formal education centre (www.inovatiruslenis.lt). Volunteers will help in a practical and creative way to develop these unique place as co-working and co-living hub in the nature. NGO Innovators' valley and DC Pangeya Ultima have been partners since 2015 and during this time many young people tried themselves in Lithuania (you can read about their experience in our blog).
Food and accommodation:

The volunteers will live in a common room formed by 2 or 3 people for each room. The volunteers will have to share the shower, toilet and fully equipped kitchen with other volunteers. During this month we will explore nature and go to the forest for some adventure camping. The organization will provide tents, sleeping bags and all the necessary for a good camping experience.
Pocket Money:
The volunteer will have 4 € per day of pocket money (120 Eur) and food money (120 Eur); the payment will be at the beginning of the month.
Why the Garden?
During this camp, we want to design and realize the area of the monastery garden.

The monastery has a long history and we want to create a space for the people and the local community where to gather, enjoy the beauty of the place, learn and practice about plants, herbs and ecology.

Шукаємо учасників на молодіжний обмін під назвою "Let's Map It" у Північній Македонії 13-21 Липня 2022р за програмою ЕРАСМУС ПЛЮС.
Довідка:

Молодіжний обмін "Let's Map It" було перенесено у Північну Македонії після підлого вторгнення росії в Україну, але ми раді, що наша молодь все-таки зможе насолодитись міжнародною компанією та поспілкуватись про основну тему проєкту: міжкультурний діалог та креативні волонтерські проєкти у сільській місцевості. Тематика та методика зустрічі заснована на проєкті Пангеї Ультіма "Image Mapping" (www.imagemapping.org).
Учасники:

До участі запрошуються українці віком 18-30 років (керівник групи може бути старше 30ти) - збираємо групу із шести учасників. Учасник має мати закордонний паспорт та можливість виїхати за кордон в умовах військового стану. Ми очікуємо, що учасники будуть зацікавлені у тематиці неформальної освіти та володіти хоча б на середньому рівні англійською мовою (це робоча мова у проєкті).
Разом із українцями у обміні візьмуть учасники із (загалом 31 учасник):
- Північної Македонії
- Швеції
- Італії
- Грузії
Місце проведення:

Молодіжний обмін відбудеться у місті Крушево, Північна Македонія, у гірській місцевості. Тому ми вважаємо це чудовою нагодою насолодитись природою цієї чудової Балканської країни. Місцевий партнер у проєкті, що реалізовуватиме програму: CET Македония.
Практичне забезпечення:

Учасникам буде покриватись - проїзд на/з проєкту у розмірі до 275 Євро на людину (згідно вартості квитків, котрі потрібно буде узгодити із організаторами); на місці буде забезпечено безкоштовну програму заходу, безкоштовне проживання у готелі та безкоштовне триразове харчування.
Не покриватимуться витрати на страхування та витрати пов'язані із COVID-регуляціями (проте у П. Македонії будь-які обмеження пов'язані із COVID були зняті).
Щоб отримати компенсацію та повне забезпечення учасники мають прийняти активну участь у всіх елементах програми!
Під час обміну учасники представлятимуть свої національні культури, тому просимо українців гідно представити Батьківщину.
Як прийняти участь:
Якщо ви хочете прийняти участь у цьому молодіжному, будь ласка, заповніть цю форму на участь: https://forms.gle/jTwh9msMgeYLUbPJ7
Якщо у вас будуть додаткові питання, будь ласка, задавайте їх на емейл pangeyaultimadc@gmail.com, або у Телеграм +380976402756.
Більше інформації у INFOPACK від наших закордонних партнерів (проте, будь ласка, використовуйте нашу форму для подачі, а не інтегровану у документ).

Ми будемо відбирати людей за пріоритетом часу подачі - в першу чергу тих, хто подав заявки раніше, тому не тягніть і заповнюйте форму вже зараз! Також ми будемо надавати перевагу жителям Вінниці та Вінницького регіону, а також внутрішньо-переселеним особам. Також можлива участь українців, котрі через зрозумілі всім обставини вже опинились неподалік місця проведення обміну - на Балканах.

title: My Volunteering experience on the Greek Island: involvement into local community and Solidarity tracks

data.text: The most important I learned about Volunteering is sharing. Sharing of your experience, knowledge, skills, time and willing. The more you give, the more you have. The act of giving creates a multiplier effect, adding something to the life of those in need but also intrinsically rewarding the giver too, making him or her happier as well.

In this article I will share my experience of volunteering for the European Solidarity Corps in the project “Sustainable Development”, organized by the Greek organization “Solidarity Tracks”. It was an Individual volunteering for 2 months, started from the end of March. I would like to Thank my sending Ukrainian organization “Pangeya Ultima”, especially Oleksandra Honcharuk for the support, taking care with all organisational issues and help with documentation during the Volunteering.

My Volunteering took part at Greek resort Lefkada, which is recognized as one of the most picturesque in the country. The island got its name (Lefkada means "white") due to the steep white rocks along the West coast. The island is part of the Ionian archipelago, famous for its white beaches and emerald crystal-clear sea waters. So, I got a chance to see 2 different moods of the area: April with low season, rains and empty streets, and then May, when everything started to come alive, blossom and getting ready for a tourist season.
Cultural Integration

In special occasion of Easter we created a postcards for the Elderly Care Center of Lefkada. Within the workshops we painted cards with ornaments using colored pencils, paper, paint and other art supplies. In such a way we created something unique and special with a warm touch of our creativity and wonderful Easter spirit. There is a tradition of carrying candles to the church for the Resurrection of Christ, usually candles are with a huge variety of colours and designs. Thus, we decorated candles making a unique self-made artwork and sharing our creativity.

I was a part of the team community Mural Painting at Nydri Primary School. The event was organized by the association Melanydros together with Amaka, Solidarity Tracks and Goodness Tour. We used art as a tool for healing and social support and created a joint Odyssey-themed mural.

Our team visited the traditional annual concert of the Music School of Lefkada. Young musicians presented the work done in the ensemble during the school year, mixing traditional and art, Western and Eastern music through well-known melodies.

I joined the Art exhibition "Dream Points" by Greek visual artist Babis Pilarinos, organized by the Cultural Center of the Municipality of Lefkada. Art works of Babis Pylarinos lead to an invisible, an inward-textured associative landscape. He use a gentle light, which does not blind but caresses the eye, spreads diffused without casting, threatening shadows and reveals hidden aspects of ourselves, dripping with nostalgia. Interior landscapes of our childhood and aromas forgotten by reaped wheat, by half-lit and wet arches, a dance voluptuous of the senses. The painting of Pylarinos, like a warm summer rain, submits the materiality through the incarnation, takes flesh from the dream and transforms it into an image.

I even felt myself more Lefkadian while wearing traditional folk costume of an island. It's characterized by simplicity, unpretentious and elegant line. The traditional costume consists of a very long pleated dress with long sleeves that is open at the front. The ‘Kotolo’, a thick petty coat is worn underneath. A padded wooden board, the ‘Spaletta’ is still used to support the chest and a long scarf to cover the bare area at the front. The front of the dress used to be decorated by attaching gold chains with ornate pins into the ‘Spaletta’ through the scarf, this also held the scarf in place. The ‘Kefalopani’, a long headscarf, covered the heads. The most beautiful was the wedding gown as usually its made of silk in bright colours.

To understand the customs and traditions of island I visited the Cultural Centre of Lefkada and Folklore Museum of Karia. In Cultural Center I was impressed by collection of traditional dress not only Greek but also other countries and even Ukrainian. Also, I checked the historical center, art gallery, Ex-Libris room and archeological exposition.

I went to the island mountains to visit the Folklore Museum of Karia Village. The Museum honors the creativity and vitality of unique “Karsaniki stitch” embroidery style of Maria Standraka, who made it only with a one hand. I’ve been admired not only of handmade exhibits, but also collection of old objects and furniture which remind a traditional house of mountainous Lefkada.
Activities and involvement

Within the activities of my organization I've been involved into local community in order to promote a cultural approach to sustainable development, implementing awareness campaigns to mobilize and convince components of the society of Lefkas for different areas of the challenges. Within the International Day of Sport for Development and Peace, Solidarity Tracks I held an activity “Accessible Sport For Everyone” on one of the central squares of Lefkas. We brought people together giving an opportunity to try different sports exercises just open air. Within the Sport session I wanted to show the positive role sport and physical activity play in communities and in people’s lives. Sport has fundamental rights and a powerful tool to strengthen social ties and promote sustainable development and peace, as well as solidarity and respect for all. To start doing exercises does not require much time, special equipment, amount of money or any additional things.

We launched the Art & Cycle Project "Solidarity Trails: cycling around the Lefkada lagoon". The event was attended by more than 50 people (locals and international volunteers). The main aim of the event was to promote cycling activity as an alternative way of sustainable development of Lefkada island and as a means of social integration and acceptance of all different social groups. Within the event we organized an artistic workshop for decorating bicycles with paper, balloons and fabrics. The cycling route around the lagoon (approximately 8 km) passed with the help of the Municipality and the Police of Lefkada.

As my organization provides an on-line educational support for the ESC volunteers, I successfully completed e-learning courses and got a Certification on Social Activism and Social Entrepreneurship, Public Speaking and Leadership, Visual Art, Emotional management and ESC Volunteering. The courses explain how to address real social problems in your community, how to find solutions, it provides skills, the tools and methods to create innovative ideas. Also, you could ask expert database with all the relevant issues. The study was instantaneous, a lot of interactive, useful tips and practical tasks. I definitely recommend it to all. Check more information at e-learning.youtheclub.eu, esc2learn.org, learn2volunteer.com

I’ve been involved into “Time Bank”, a network for exchanging services and knowledge (know-how), supported by the Solidarity Tracks. It forms a mutual exchange of services and knowledge on the scale of a local community. Here you can share your competences and knowledge and offer your time, under the form of services with regard to your skills. You are entitled to receive other services, on a mutual basis, according to your needs and wishes.

We held a dissimination event in Lefkada Cultural center to present the results of the Project “Сlandestine immigration: Awareness & Inclusion through ART” in order to raise the public’s awareness about the danger of clandestine immigration. The main aim of the Project was to develop a new skill in order to support young people from immigrant background or wishing to emigrate in the frame of the human rights values. Through the all Project stages we raised awareness against illegal immigration via theater practices, created tools & innovative methods of education about immigration through art and theater and developed a professional network between Euro Med youth workers. We organized intercultural workshops on the study of the Greek language and history, Ukrainian culture and traditions in Basque Country, breaking the stereotypes about Spain. I maintained the social media of my organization. In particular, I wrote a posts on “Green O’Clock” page – Greece online magazine blog about actual events and activities in Lefkada, linked with sustainable development.
Support for Ukraine

Solidarity with Ukraine I felt everywhere: from people, activities and even buildings with Ukrainian flags. I gathered all concerned people in Lefkada to show Solidarity with Ukraine through Art. Within activity “Art As A Tool For Creative Learning” I told more about Ukrainian culture, attributes and the current situation in my home city, Kyiv. Together with volunteers from France, Latvia, Tunisia, Italy, Spain, Slovenia, we created an art exhibition expressing our Support and Wishes for Ukrainians who are facing a difficult time now. In addition, we held creative meetings with three groups of children from Lefkada. Greek kids created 3 posters in order to support Ukrainian children: 1) on the topic of Peace, with a collage of Ukrainian attributes and the main symbol – Doves; 2) on the topic of Solidarity by creating a map of Ukraine; 3) a tree of life with wishes of peace, strengths and health. After, we created an exhibition of all paintings and sent all the messages to Ukraine with a hope for a peace in Ukraine.
Conclusion

I’m grateful to “Solidarity Tracks”, especially Mohamed Chaabouni, Alexia and Ioanna for the opportunity to become a part of the Project, for the hospitable and warm welcoming, support, solidarity and high level of Volunteering. Don’t wait for a change, make it happen! Just follow your heart, do something noble and beautiful, awake and start live the full life from today.
The article was prepared by Sana Lisova - journalist, researcher, public activist

title: How Masha Yuzkova was a job shadower in Gençlik Çalışmaları Derneği!

data.text: We are glad to present you how Masha Yuzkova was a job shadower in Gençlik Çalışmaları Derneği :

Although I already took part in Erasmus youth exchanges and trainings before, this experience was very new to me. I was integrated not only in organizations activities but the lives of people who work there. This is also the longest project I have ever been to, which is 17 days. The program was built in a way to integrate participants fully and still not to overload us with information and activities. Due to the circumstances we all live in, it is very important to consider resources and the amount of energy each person can contribute. I felt included, safe and grateful.
We visited:
- Municipality which is also a hub for young people where they come, get support and a team that focuses on their topic and can share expertise;
- Association that helps children with SMA. There we created figures from plaster (birds, vases, flowers, etc.) and painted them for future charity event. It was an enjoyable team building activity;

- Gönüllü Hareketi Derneği organization where people could speak English and that made that visit a very productive one. They told us about its origin and founders’ background, what projects they organize, and how they work with volunteers. They have their own studio where they create audio books for people with special needs, a toy library, a food bank, etc. They also work with Erasmus+ and ESC.

*As an option for cooperation, our organization and this association can apply for a grant to create an app similar to ‘Too good to go’ which is used in Europe and USA. In this app shops, cafes, and bakeries post the food which is about to spoil, and people who would like to get it, go to these places and get this food with a discount. So the food is saved and people are fed. :) The grant will help to hire IT people and the marketing team who helps with this project.
- We visited the organization where people with special needs are engaged. I was happy to present ГО "Гармонія" and share there experience to somehow inspire.

After all the visits we`ve been working on activities for Dlabs for youngsters on emloyability and soft skills that will take place in Mudanya in August. Our main focus was to implement tools of non formal education and I think we did a good job together. Other thing to mention is an amazing place we were staying. Mudanya is a small picturesque city that I loved with all my heart. Working in such a beautiful place is a special experience. For those of you planning to apply, be aware that not many people speak english, but there is always a way to communicate. You just have to be patient and open-minded.

title: Open Kitchen 2.0 - a Youth Exchange in Antaliepte, Lithuania

data.text:
Youth exchange "Open Kitchen 2.0" was planned to be in Ukraine, in Vinnytsia. But we all know why it's not possible now. So the best decision was to make it in Antaliepte, Lithuania. And, to be honest, it was an amazing time.
38 participants from Lithuania, Latvia and Ukraine came to a little village Antaliepte to get unforgettable experience, to get new knowledge and to create a cook book as a result of the teamwork.
We also learned how to make designs, shoot photos and make tasty healthy food. Each of the groups had different tasks, and they had professionals in their fields that could teach a lot of new things.

This project touched us in so many ways. All together we were enjoying communication, community of young active people, sharing experience, learning new things every single day. Meeting people with whom you have a lot of similarities, meeting people who has completely different experience, exploring the world together, creating sincere atmosphere where you can be yourself. Improving the skills in communication, photography, cooking and design. Getting new experience working as a team. Sharing your own experience in different fields. Actively participating in every day reflection as a time to share feelings and emotions you felt during the day, time for yourself and time in society with other people. Trying to live and to not be "around the news" as often, but at the same time knowing what is going on, to let yourself feel the emotions, live them and let them go...
Fresh herbal tea, collected by participants and made with love for the breakfast and lunch. Delicious meals and greetings "Enjoy your meal!" in at least 5 different languages.

Late musical evenings with a sound of guitar, secret (or not secret) messages in the envelopes, walking near the water mill, deep conversations, each other support. Fun time near the lakes - swimming, chatting, trying to survive lovely bites of mosquitoes and finding wild berries.
Learning new things about other countries and their culture through the dialogue and intercultural evenings.
The atmosphere of the monastery we were living made an impact for the whole project.
It was time to relax and to work at the same time. To switch a bit from a usual everyday life and gather motivation to improve yourself and make this world better in many different ways. It was an opportunity to ask yourself many different questions and try to search for an answer. Not always the answers we uncover is the ones we like to share, but it's also a way to learn about acception.

This project was filled with lots of support, love and openness. With funny moments and energizers. With challenges and motivation. Sometimes with sadness. With creativity. With rain. Days were so active, sometimes you didn't even have time to check your phone and answer the messages. Sometimes you didn't even want to check them, because you wanted to be in the moment here and now. Sometimes you really wanted to share some moments with friends who is not with you now.
A lot of things happened during one week of the project. But the word I would like to sum it all up - it's unity.

title: Відгук Анни про молодіжний обмін "Lat's map it" в Північній Македонії.

data.text: Відгук Анни про молодіжний обмін "Lat's map it" в Північній Македонії.

Привіт! Мене звати Аня. Я з міста Суми, зараз тимчасово проживаю у Празі. Хочу поділитися своїм досвідом та враженнями з молодіжного обміну Erasmus+ у Крушево, Північна Македонія на тему “Let’s Map It! Intercultural dialogue in countryside areas”.

По-перше, мене дуже вразила країна, а, особливо, місце, в якому проходив обмін. Місто Крушево побудоване у формі амфітеатру і знаходиться у горах. Під час проєкту були дуже сонячні дні, тому це стало прекрасною можливістю досліджувати природу і знайти те саме місце, яке ми обрали визначним. Невдовзі там буде встановлено рамку з описом пам’ятки, який теж підготувала Еразмус-група.
По-друге, я неймовірно задоволена нашою командою. Мені було цікаво проводити час з іноземною активною молоддю і представляти українську культуру разом з іншими учасницями з національної групи.

Це були яскраві дні, наповнені веселощами і в той же час продуктивними тренінгами і завданнями, я вдосталь насолодилася природою і спілкуванням. Я би хотіла, щоб молодіжний обмін тривав довше. Це один з найкращих проєктів у моєму житті, адже я відпочила душею, одночасно виконуючи добру справу.
Дякую українській організації “Pangeya Ultima” за таку неймовірну можливість!

title: Відгук Ольги Бовкун про молодіжний обмін "Lat's map it" в Північній Македонії

data.text: Відгук Ольги Бовкун про молодіжний обмін "Lat's map it" в Північній Македонії.
Це був важливий досвід для мене. Перш за все - це досвід міжнародної дипломатії, занурення в культуру іншої країни та обмін ідеями щодо зеленого туризму між країнами.

Учасники команди, як української, так і міжнародної були унікальними, яскравими особистостями, зі своїми культурно-історичними розбіжностями. Ми всі були страшенно різними, але ми з задоволенням провели час разом, а почуття гумору зробило нас ще більш дружніми. Шкодую, що часу було не так багато, щоб побільше познайомитися з ними.
Дякую Бояну за привітність і гостинність, тепер Крушево для мене одне з найкращих місць на планеті. Дякую кожному тім-ліду, ви зробити з нас команду! Це талант!
Я після проекту відчуваю натхнення на дещо нове і дякую всім причетним до цього!
Дякую за проект Pangea Ultima, Let’s Map It, Erasmus+.
#imagemapping

title: Відгук Вікторії Антре про молодіжний обмін "Lat's map it" в Північній Македонії

data.text: Відгук Вікторії Антре про молодіжний обмін "Lat's map it" в Північній Македонії.
Для мене першочерговим в Ерасмус + завжди були люди. Нові знайомства, думки, ідеї. Зміни у мені, зміни, викликані мною.

Та цього разу першочерговим став інший аспект. Ідучи в Північну Македонію, я про неї знала лише за суперечкою про назву країни. Покидаючи її - я мала повне уявлення про країну, світогляд її мешканців, розташування, туристичні принади і непривабливу сторону життя теж.
А зараз, пишучи відгук, усвідомила, що назва проекту "Let's map it" застерігала з самого початку.

Пазл склався. І прийшло усвідомлення для чого цей проект. Словами можна відкрити лише верхній шар - "нетуристичні" місця, дають змогу заглянути всередину себе і знайти там значно більше ніж ви могли б очікувати. Ніж я могла б очікувати. І цей зовсім новий пласт викликає цікавість - а що там ще є.
Тому відкривайте для себе нові місця. Туристичні і не дуже. Заглядайте вглиб і діліться власним всесвітом. І змінюйте. Вам же прийшла думка, що ви хотіли б змінити?
Дякую Пангея Ультім і Ерасмус+.
#imagemapping

title: Привіт! Я - Оля, завдяки можливості від Пангеї Ультіма відвідала

data.text: Привіт! Я - Оля, завдяки можливості від Пангеї Ультіма відвідала Македонію та взяла участь в проекті "Image Mapping". Хоча, по правді кажучи, це не перша моя участь в цьому проекті ;)

На 2022-ий рік у мене, як і у більшості молоді, було багато планів на подорожі, відвідування нових країн, проте повномасштабне вторгнення росії зіпсувало ці плани. Емоційно та фізично війна дається важко, навіть коли ти знаходишся у відносно безпечному місті, тому я на котрий місяць війни була відверто кажучи втомлена, адже також багато працювала весь цей час. Одного дня натрапила на оголошення про пошук учасників на проект та подумала, що це саме цей шанс поєднати декілька речей: відвідати нову країну, відволіктись і відпочити, приєднатись до "Image Mapping" ще раз.

Класично, на такому проекті ми (учасники обміну) мали б будувати місце з такою собі рамкою та лавочкою для олгяду якоїсь цікавої місцини. Морально я готувалась до того, що треба буде будувати, фарбувати, розчищати, а по факту ніби поїхала у відпустку!

По-перше, Македонія дуже славна і красива країна, зокрема гірське курортне містечко Крушево, в якому ми перебували. Місцеві жителі надзвичайно привітні, багато з них володіють англійською мовою, тож вцілому перебування там було супер-комфортним.

По-друге, на обмін приїхали просто неймовірно класні учасники з Італії, Швеції, Македонії і звісно ж з України. Була досить дружня атмосфера, хоча й всі були різного віку. Ми легко спілкувались одне з одним, обмінювались культурними різницями та особливостями наших країн. В свою чергу, ми - дівчата з України, мали змогу представити нашу країну, наші теперішні реалії життя. Радує, що абослютно всі учасники обміну вже знали про Україну, спілкувались раніше з українцями та знають про військове вторгнення з боку росії. По закінченню обміну, я розумію, що здобула дуже кльові нові знайомтсва.

По-третє, сам обмін видався цікавим по наповненню. Так, ми не будували класичного оглядового місця, проте досить багато спілкувались з місцевими, розпитували про їх історію, про життя в містечку Крушево. Так, один із місуевих чоловіків люб'язно нам відчинив колишню школц, яка тепер слугує місуевим театром та таким собі молодіжним простором. Також, нам неймовірно пощастило перебувати в Крушево в часі чемпіонату світу з парапланеризму (параглайдингу), тож ми також мали змогу поспілкуватись з спортсменами з усього світу, почути мотиваційну промову від одного з орагнізаторів змагань та побачити неймовірний старт парапланеристів (близько 100+ парапланеристів, які взлітають майже одночасно).
Найбільше з цієї подорожі мені запам'ятались теплі обійми, щирі розмови і надзвичайні люди ❤️
Тож, щиро запрошую молодь не ловити гав, а подаватись на проекти Erasmus+. А якщо є питання, чи потреба в підтримці, то завжди можна звернутись до Пангеї Ультіма.

title: Відгук Анастасії про молодіжний обмін 'Let's map it' у Північній

data.text: Відгук Анастасії про молодіжний обмін 'Let's map it' у Північній Македонії
Вітаю! Мене звати Анастасія, і сьогодні я б хотіла поділитися враженнями від короткого Еразмус+ обміну, у якому брала участь 13-21 липня.

Моїм найбільшим враженням є неймовірна гостинність Північної Македонії - у столиці Скоп'є, у місці обміну високогірному містечку Крушево, у туристичному Охриді - всюди мене зустрічали теплі, привітні люди, і бути там було просто і легко. Країна сонячна і гориста, і вона має багато куточків, у яких хочеться залишитися з блокнотом на цілий день. Крушево, зокремо, сподобається любителям і любителькам висоти, свободи й тиші.

На обміні ми багато говорили про розуміння цінності місцевості, про необхідність зупинитися, щоб усвідомити цінність - про це ідея мепінгу, яку ми впроваджували в Крушево. Прагнення заземлитися, не сприймати як даність, а дивитися натомість туристичними очима мені дуже близьке, бо я проходила той самий шлях зі своїм рідним містом і з іншими містами, у яких жила. Це вимагає початкового зусилля, але нагороджує задоволенням від життя в своєму місті, містечку чи селі.

Я задоволена спілкуванням з учасниками й учасницями, бо з різним віком і бекґраундом усі ми були дуже відкриті до спілкування й обміну досвідами. Рада, що мали можливість говорити про Україну не лише формально, а й справді розказати про війну і життя, що завжди перемагає, організували благодійний концерт вінницького гурту (дякую Ярославу, Каті і Жені), який зустріли дуже сердечно, ліпили вареники і співали разом. Від цього стає тепло.
Вдячна Ungdomsfronten, CET PLATFORMA Skopje, Pangeya Ultima.

title: Короткостроковий Еразмус-обмін в Македонії став великим відкриттям

data.text: Короткостроковий Еразмус-обмін в Македонії став великим відкриттям для мене. Не знаю, чи випала б у найближчому майбутньому ще така нагода зануритися в македонську культуру, закохатися раз і назавжди в балканські ландшафти, вивчати історію міста Крушево. А щонайважливіше – познайомитися з прекрасними людьми зі Швеції, Македонії, Італії, Індії, Палестини і Сирії.

Перед собою я також ставила завдання розповісти іноземним друзям про те, що відбувається в Україні зараз, привернути увагу до необхідності підтримувати нашу країну в нелегкий час. Для мене виявилося несподіванкою, що Україна має тісні зв’язки з Македонією ще з кінця 90-х років, коли уклала Договір про дружбу та співробітництво. У свою чергу наша держава доклала необхідних зусиль для збереження цілісності Македонії на початку 2000-х, коли та мала збройне протистояння з Албанією. Тому цей обмін не лише про проєкт “Let’s map it,” а й про роль культурної дипломатії, яка конче потрібна Україні сьогодні.

Повертаючись до теми обміну – міжкультурний діалог та волонтерські проєкти в сільській місцевості, я хочу зазначити, що Крушево – це найкраще місце для проведення даного заходу. Містечко, попри відсутність усієї необхідної інфраструктури на даний момент, має великий потенціал стати однією з найпривабливіших локацій на туристичній мапі південної Європи. Цінний кейс для мене, враховуючи те, що незабаром буду вивчати туризм! Вдячна організаторам проєкту, Erasmus+ за можливість неформального навчання та розширення власних горизонтів.
Софія Стрілець

title: The story of the turbulent and effective ESC of Franziska Barthele

data.text: I come from Germany, from the beautiful Lake of Constance. But I only wanted to get away from there early on, first to Berlin to study environmental computing. After that, I did a voluntary service in Benin, West Africa, with the German exchange program weltwärts. During that time I was able to learn a lot, so that I was drawn to France for my next studies with Erasmus, and then to Ukraine with the ESC program. I missed the volunteer work, I wanted to learn a Slavic language, and thought the exchange with countries that are not yet in the EU makes more sense. And so quickly you end up in Vinnytsia, a beautiful university town in central Ukraine, and in the NGO Pangeya Ultima, which got a family to me.
My first weekend in Vinnytsia, we already shot a video to learn ukrainian language: Rémy, Olha, Juliusz, me, Ibrahim

In Vinnytsia, my tasks were very diverse. Once a week I organized a German course with my fellow volunteer Juliusz, which was also a lot about teaching the German culture. On some weekends we were in the village "Stina" and did different works at the EkoCenter of Pangeya Ultima. That was really exciting, because also in Ukraine life in the countryside is very different from city life. I also participated in the Intercultural Magazine "Mozaika", and spread the word about the possibilities of the Erasmus and ESK world in different ways. I was also able to establish the Pangeya Youth Club with my fellow volunteer David. Here we met regularly with young people from Vinnytsia and played, talked and laughed together, thus enabling the young people in Vinnytsia to make use of their English skills in a playful way.
I, Jules, Igor in Pangeya Youth Club, engaged in the game

In February we also had a big celebration of the 10th birthday of Pangeya Ultima, together with many guests. With Juliusz and others we also practiced Ukrainian folk music and performed a song that evening. It was a nice big celebration, with many guests. In the western press at that time there were already many warnings about security in Ukraine. However, no one on the ground wanted to believe that, everyone was used to provocations from the Russian side.

In Ukraine, I quickly gained a different approach to the subject of war, because of what is happening in the country since 2014. Even though Vinnytsia was far away from the front, the topic was still present and I learned to look at it from a different perspective. In Germany, national pride is almost a taboo because of our history, but it is a completely different situation in Ukraine. With the beginning of the war due to the invasion of Russia, I quickly left the country with other volunteers. This was already planned in advance with Pangeya Ultima as well as NaturKultur in Germany out of caution, and I was also supported in the best possible way by both sides at that moment. The war turned many things upside down for me. That something like this could happen in 21st century Europe was unimaginable. But I was quickly safe and "only" had to worry about friends, not my family. The suffering of the Ukrainians is unimaginable.

Back at my parents' home on Lake Constance, I continued my voluntary service, now in helping refugees. If I couldn't help my local friends, I could at least help their compatriots who had ended up in my home country.

My new tasks were now, as before, to give German lessons. Now, however, in a completely different context, even though most of my audience were Ukrainians again. I also helped in a primary school preparation for refugee children from Syria and Afghanistan. Here, my basic knowledge of Ukrainian did me no good, and I practiced communication through hands, feet, pointing and demonstrating. Soon I also joined the weekly Ukraine café run by Caritas Konstanz. Here I helped in the café operation, but also helped the integration managers fill out applications as needed. Here I was able to get a good insight from my colleagues about what people have to do upon arrival, and especially what a bureaucratic hell they have to go through. In addition, I was able to help some Ukrainians with small services, for example, the organization of a doctor's appointment, the mediation of addresses where there are cheap clothes and things of daily use, or in the communication on eBay-kleinanzeigen.de (german OLX).

I was able to put all this new knowledge to good use when I continued my commitment in my village, on the island of Reichenau. There I was able to help in the town hall with my language skills, and from this some cooperations developed. Through an appeal in the local newspaper, I found some volunteer language helpers with whom we were able to establish a simple German course. That was a first success, which also helped me to find a German teacher, who is now doing an integration course in cooperation with the VHS in the town hall of Reichenau. This is a great relief, because the way by public transport to the next city with German courses is really complicated for the refugees. Here I would like to thank again all the volunteers at Reichenau, without you all this would not have been possible. Through the first German courses, the first friendships have already formed, and integration into the local associations is also beginning.

Mary from Pangeya Ultima has found a temporary new home in Berlin because of the war. There I visited her and her children Zorjana and Miroslav. Seeing friends from life before the war again was an incredibly beautiful moment, albeit with a ghastly background.

When I was working in Germany, I often didn't know what would be a good next step. So I tried a lot of different things, was very proactive, and even if not everything I imagined worked out, I was able to make a difference.
Overall, I learned more than I could list, but here's a little insight:
• teach german (on a low level)
• understand and speak Ukrainian (not a high level, but still very helpful)
• I have intensively dealt with the topic of war and have discarded old ways of thinking.
• got an insight into the reality of Ukrainian life and how they deal with their Soviet history, as well as with their history as a country exploited and colonized from different sides
• an insight into issues of sustainability in Ukraine: e.g. waste, renewable energy and illegal deforestation
• The possibilities of "active citizenship" → what is needed in society, and how can I contribute?
• acting proactively, asking different institutions for cooperation
• get an insight into the German bureaucratic world of asylum application/ residence permit/ social benefit application as well as the guidelines for BAMF-funded integration courses
• Start calls for help, use appropriate means (e.g. local newspaper) for it
• Find motivation in situations where one feels incredibly helpless.

I applied for the ESC program because I wanted to go abroad again and learn a new language. Now I'm also glad to have continued the service in Germany, because I got an intensive insight into the situation of refugees who have just arrived in Germany. Here it was partly nice to see what infrastructure already existed here (mostly since the refugee wave of 2015), but partly also frightening what is not covered, and with how many things people are left alone. Moreover, any engagement was always difficult with the background of a 2-class structure between the refugees from Ukraine and the refugees from other countries.

Even though I don't wish anyone such a turbulent year as my last year, I would recommend the ESC volunteer service to everyone. You don't necessarily learn what you expect to learn beforehand, you rather broaden your horizon so much that you are able to ask even more valuable questions afterwards than before.

In Ukraine it was too cold for me to travel in winter, so apart from Vinnytsia and Stina I only saw a small part of Kyiv. Lviv, Kharkiv, Odessa, Mariupol and so many other cities and regions I wanted to visit in the summer are now inaccessible, partly badly destroyed. With my many new Ukrainian acquaintances I hope that one day we can meet again in their hometowns. And that they can then show me their homeland, after I have helped them to get along in my homeland. It is sad that Ukraine is now only associated with war and suffering, when I had such a wonderful time in this huge, beautiful, and diverse country.
Слава Україні!
Franziska Bärthele

title: Відгук Ірини про її досвід волонтерства в екоцентрі в Хорватії

data.text: It's been 3,5 months since I came to eko-centar Latinovac in Croatia. I want to share my experience and impressions here.
I was volunteering at the eko-centar Latinovac , which is located in a small village in Croatia.

Before the project I was doubted a lot. I was not sure if I should really go to this place, I almost didn't know what to expect from local people and the village. I was not sure if I would be fine in this place. I was not sure that I could be here for such a long period of time. I had quite a lot of fears in my head because it is my first project and first time going abroad alone. Nevertheless I managed my hesitation because I really wanted to change my life.

One of the main reasons to try the project was practicing English. Volunteering gave me a chance to improve my language skills. Before the project I had a language barrier. I was anxious when I spoke to someone in English. Sometimes it was difficult to talk with foreigners and to understand them. Now I can express my thoughts more fluently, that is very important for me. I feel the difference in my listening skills, too. During the project you face people from different places and with different accents. I remember the first day when I arrived here I met my roommate from Spain. We started to talk to get to know each other more but, honestly, I barely understood even half of her speech. Now I don't have problems with that. Moreover, I had a chance to learn some words and expressions in other languages like French, Spanish, Turkish, Portugal, German and, of course, Croatian. I even started to understand local people.

Also, this place gave me a lot of new meetings and friends. During volunteering I met 2 groups of short term volunteers. It's great to have the opportunity to meet new, interesting and different people. I`m sure that with some of them I`ll keep in touch for a long time after the project.

My work here was often connected with kids. We organized and visited some festivals. We prepared activities for children. Usually it was dancing, sport and language games. Besides that, we worked in our garden with our plants, helped with repairing some things on our property. Also, from time to time we helped local people on the farm. Our work was diverse. So, some days we had skill sharing activities, workshops, hiking, and visiting other organizations.

Also, I was interested in ecology before the project. So I had an opportunity to find out more about it. I learned new things about gardening and I discovered that I really like it. Moreover, we had lectures about sustainability and permaculture. Probably, It's something that I didn't hear earlier. The fact that these lectures are not boring because the material is presented is very good.

By the way, the nature in Croatia is amazing. I love mountains so much and I`m so happy that I had a chance to live here. During our free days we had the opportunity to travel together around the country. I visited cities like Zagreb, Pula, Zadar, Slavonski Brod and other towns close to our place. I saw the best sunsets in my life in Croatia.

About coordinators. Honestly, they are some of the nicest people I've met. I`m so lucky to meet them. They care about this place and people here so much. They are very good examples for me that show how to love the work they do.

Of course, sometimes it was very challenging for me to live here because I had never lived in the village before. I couldn't even think that It can happen to me. But I changed my opinion about living in the countryside and I see that it can be very cool. I also often worked on leaving my comfort zone. I had quite a lot of situations when I had to talk to strangers for help. That's why I became more communicative and opened to new meetings. I can definitely say that local people are always ready to help you, especially if they know you`re from Ukraine. They are very nice.
The project opened new interests for me that I`ll continue doing after the project. I feel how much I changed here. I'm more confident in myself.

I love this place so much. This place is so peaceful . Here everything is made for you to feel good. The place where you forget about your problems, where you don't chase for something. You just enjoy the moment and can allow yourself to go with the flow. You can concentrate on yourself and find what you really like.
One of my favorite things that we used to do is have a bonfire. We spent the whole evening there discussing various topics. I`ll miss that cozy atmosphere and this nice tradition.
Now, I am very motivated to try new projects in other countries. Especially I want to go deeper in the field of sustainable living.

This amazing experience from Latinovac will stay forever in my heart. I`ll miss this place and coordinators so much. I would definitely recommend this project to others. Latinovac is a great opportunity for youth and especially for people who don't know what to do in life or trying to find themselves.
Iryna Derkach

title: Відгук Ані - учасниці молодіжного обміну 'Let's Plant Stop Smog` (18-27 вересня)

data.text: Мене звати Аня і я щойно повернулась додому з Польщі з молодіжного обміну 'Let's Plant Stop Smog`, на який потрапила завдяки програмі Erazmus+ та організації NGO “Pangeya ultima”.

Скажу абсолютно відверто, один шматочок моєї душі ще і досі знаходиться у Польщі, а інший шматочок поїхав автобусом до Словенії з моїми новими друзями, яких я знайшла завдяки цій поїздці. Я безмежно вдячна за таку неймовірну можливість, за цікавий досвід та незабутні емоції. Я дуже щаслива, що була маленькою частинкою цього нереального проєкту.

За такий короткий термін часу (18-27 вересня) я змогла помітно покращити свої мовні навички, знайшла в собі абсолютно нові сторони, які допомогли мені у спілкуванні, відкрила для себе безліч нових та цікавих фактів про інші країни та їх культуру, а найголовніше - ознайомилась з деякими пунктами надважливої наразі для всіх теми - екологічного способу життя.

Зі свого боку можу сказати, що ми, з нашою чудовою групою українських дівчат, приклали максимум зусиль для того, аби іноземці дізнались багато цікавого про українську культуру, історію та в цілому про те, що, на жаль, відбувається зараз.
Проєкт подарував мені враження на все життя, нових чудових друзів і безцінний досвід, який мені знадобиться ще не раз.

title: Відгук Анастасії - учасниці молодіжного обміну 'Let's Plant Stop Smog` (18-27 вересня)

data.text: Мене звати Настя і нещодавно я повернулася додому з проєкту Erasmus+ "Let's Plant - Stop Smog" в Польщі.
Я брала участь у підготовчій зустрічі до самого обміну, а також у самому обміні.
Гори, воркшопи, розмови до ранку, stepping out of the comfort zone і відкриття своїх нових талантів - коротко про мій Еразмус.

Організатори надали нам можливість самостійно організовувати частку воркшопів, тобто кожна команда, кожний учасник обміну присвятив себе процесу та результату проєкту. Кожний учасник почував себе частиною команди та обміну.

Тема стосувалася екології та забрудненні повітря в містах, наприклад як Катовіце, Польща. У нас була можливість дізнатися більше і про досвід наших колег, і поділитися досвідом України в данному питанні, а також дізнатися про варіанти вирішення згаданих проблем.
Досі сумую за чудовими людьми, яких зустріла під час проєкту. Організатори були відкритими і завжди готовими допомогти.
Такі обміни це неймовірно крута можливість розширити свою мережу контактів, змінити погляди на життя, відкрити новий талант. Тому запевняю читача, що воно того варте!

📍The team of organizers from the NGO "Pangaea Ultima" is sincerely happy for the success of the active participants, because in addition to the acquired knowledge, they developed their skills, found an envirnoment of like-minded people and received unique information that will contribute to their development in the professional area! 🎓👩🏻‍💻

The program was developed together with our international partners - public organizations from Moldova, Belgium, Portugal, Italy, Romania, Turkey, Armenia, Poland, Belarus, Georgia🇲🇩🇧🇪🇵🇹🇮🇹🇷🇴🇹🇷🇦🇲🇵🇱🇧🇾🇬🇪
So, below is more details about each event ☺️

The first training as part of the #developtogether project was great! 🥳

The participants also received a homework assignment that must be completed before the final class☝🏻

📆 On September 24, another training was about "Soft skills"☺️
Thanks to energisers and interesting exercises, the participants were able to get to know themselves better😉, communicate with each other and improve teamwork🤝Moreover, the participants had the opportunity to prove themselves as speakers🎙 and improve their public speaking skills 😎
As we think, it is so important to be able to speak publicly and get people interested in your topic☝🏻 These skills are very important in today's world!
- Directly from workers about the entrepreneurship and success story of the well-known in Vinnytsia "CHERDAK space" Interesting, right? ✨

This is how the 3 event of training. 🕰We spent 3 hours in a wonderful place, where the managers told us in practice about the idea, the way to implementation and interesting stories during work🏢 The participants had the opportunity to ask exciting questions directly to the employees👨‍⚖️
It is important for us not only to talk about theory 📖, but also practically show successful cases. It inspires to work and look for your own career path👩🏻‍💻
📍4th event was special for the participants, because we combined 2 very interesting topics in one event: Digital skills and Youth Mobility🌏

📆 On September 29, the participants had an online meeting about online tools of communication📲 Alla Yukhymchuk shared new information about the leading social networks, personal brand and sales. A lot of information was provided, but the most important thing is to use it! 👩🏻‍💻

🔹Moreover, Yaroslav Gerashchenko shared super-opportunities for young people here and abroad✈️: youth exchanges, trainings and international projects. He shared his experience of working in the youth community sector and inspired participation. Thanks to this, we get to know the world and ourselves! 🌏✨
📆The first of October - Graduation evening 🎓
The participants presented their achievements from classes and showed themselves in the best way!🔥
And what exactly happened, we will tell you! First of all, the participants received homework from each class:
🔹Prepare a business plan for future business

🥳 All participants showed themselves as an active person, and we are also happy to congratulate the winners Iryna Derkach, Diana Prysiazhniuk and Tanya Turchyn. They collected the most points and once again confirmed that if you work hard, you can achieve a lot! ☝🏻
To say that it was impressive is an understatement! It was incredible - energy, atmosphere and mood! 🤩
We thank the participants and the team for such a productive training! ☺️
